Education

Education Vision

Developing talent through hands-on education

SNU Robotics Institute pursues hands-on education in which students design, build and test robots themselves. We connect research equipment, spaces and the expertise of our researchers to teaching, so that students gain experience solving real problems. Through Creative Engineering Design and the Talent Development Program, we develop robotics talent with both theoretical understanding and the ability to build, and we aim for an ecosystem in which the outcomes of education carry through to research and entrepreneurship.

Creative Engineering DesignTalent Development Program

Creative Engineering Design

Creative Engineering Design is a project-based course in which first-year students in the Department of Mechanical Engineering at Seoul National University work in teams to design and build their own robots. First introduced in 1993 by the late Professor Chong Nam Chu, it has continued for more than 30 years and has become a signature engineering course at the SNU College of Engineering.

Course Description

This course aims to develop a sense of design and creativity by having students design and fabricate various objects through hands-on practice with Internet of Things (IoT) technology, which is widely used across industrial devices and home appliances including automobiles, robots, and smartphones. Building on this foundation, the course further extends to the implementation of Physical AI—artificial intelligence that perceives, reasons about, and acts upon the real world on its own. By utilizing microcontrollers (Arduino, 32-bit MCUs, etc.), students understand the basic structure of an MCU, collect data through various sensors such as temperature, humidity, light, sound, motion, and image, and learn the principles of connecting and controlling output devices such as displays and motors. On this basis, students connect objects through wired and wireless communication and implement on-device AI (TinyML), which learns and infers directly on the device, thereby completing the entire process—from sensing to reasoning and action—as a single integrated system. The course is structured so that students with little experience in coding or hardware can learn step by step from the introductory stage, and by combining theory with hands-on practice, it connects with other engineering design courses, from the fundamentals through to prototype development.

Course Objectives

This course aims to develop a basic sense of design and fabrication, as well as creativity, through hands-on design and fabrication of a variety of given targets. Intended for first-year students who have not yet formed a clear concept of engineering, it has students build products themselves from specified materials and compete with them, so that they can experience the meaning of engineering with genuine interest. The products take many forms, such as mechanisms and structures, that together reflect the characteristics of various engineering fields. During the first six weeks, lectures on basic design principles, kinematics and fabrication methods are combined with robot programming practice and fabrication. The course consists of two hours of lecture and two hours of lab each week. In week 7, the purpose and rules of the robots that students will design and build are announced, and in week 12 the main competition is held with the robots each team has freely designed and built within the given rules, using the materials and tools provided.

About the Course

Students conceive robots that carry out a given mission, then build and test them within limited conditions to solve the problem. Along the way, they develop creativity, teamwork and engineering problem-solving skills. The course content has changed steadily to reflect advances in technology, and since 2024 it has used remote-control devices as a foundation for teaching AI robot architecture.

Curriculum

Creative Engineering Design 1
Computer-aided design and software fundamentals
Creative Engineering Design 2
Robot hardware, motor control, basic circuits and building a working robot

SNU Robocon

The course culminates in Robocon, a team competition in which every student competes with the robot they built in class.

1993
First Creative Engineering Design robot competition
2022
30th anniversary of Creative Engineering Design and the 30th Robocon (Haedong Idea Factory). Winner: Team Zero; runner-up: Team Emergency Rescue; Engineering Award: Team-3; Creativity Award: Team Triple S
2024
The 32nd Robocon, held at the Haedong Advanced Engineering Building as Part 2 of SNU Robotics Day, with 60 students taking part. The winning team, “Jorip-wang” (Assembly King), earned a place in an international Robocon competition.

Student Voices

“Whenever we had an idea, we tested it, and we built our final robot from the ones that worked. When we won, I thought of everything we had been through and couldn’t hold back my tears.”

Team Zero, winner of the 30th Robocon

“We missed the title amid real-world variables, but even if we could turn back time, we couldn’t have done better. We gave it everything.”

Team Emergency Rescue, runner-up of the 30th Robocon

“Determined to win the Robocon game, we stuck together all semester and lived with the rulebook. Because we were always thinking about winning, we had more ideas than we could use.”

Team-3, semifinalist of the 30th Robocon
